newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Arabs, Israelis trade bricks, bullets in Hebron.
newsitem.headline: Arabs, Israelis trade bricks, bullets in Hebron.

text.p: Bricks, bullets and bombs flew in the West Bank town of Hebron again on Friday after street activists from PLO leader Yasser Arafat's Fatah faction failed to hold back Palestinian demonstrators, witnesses said.

"Allahu Akbar! (God is Greatest)," dozens of demonstrators shouted as they threw stones and bottles at battle-ready Israeli troops on the confrontation line between Israeli- and Palestinian-run sectors of Hebron.
Jeering demonstrators shrugged off the efforts of some 25 Fatah activists to push them back in a bid to dampen renewed violence in the volatile town.

The city's heart has been a battleground since a Jewish woman ignited Arab anger last week by pasting anti-Moslem placards depicting the Prophet Mohammad as a pig stamping on the Koran with one hoof and writing in it with another.

Witnesses said a home-made bomb exploded in Hebron's casbah in the same alley where a similar device wounded two Israeli soldiers earlier in the week. They said soldiers responded with a barrage of rubber bullets, wounding three.
Other soldiers on roofs rained stones and bottles back at protesters.

Israel sealed Hebron on Friday to try to stifle unrest, bracing for violence following weekly Moslem Friday prayers. Witnesses said Israeli troops erected roadblocks around Hebron and turned back non-residents at entrances to the volatile city.
"Since the morning, the Israeli army is preventing the entrance of Palestinians who do not live in Hebron to the (Palestinian-ruled) H1 area for security reasons," an army statement said.
Israel and the Palestinian Authority have blamed each other for the violence.

Israeli Chief Rabbi Eliahu Bakshi-Doron on Thursday met the Mufti of Hebron, the city's top Moslem cleric, to condemn the hate posters and to ask that he work to cool passions in the town holy to Moslem and Jew as the burial place of Abraham.
"Certainly, the entire Jewish people are disgusted by these deeds," Bakshi-Doron told Israel's army radio on Friday.
"I asked him to make all efforts not to fan the flames from a religious standpoint...This is a political dispute and certainly not one between Judaism and Islam."
Israeli leaders have condemned the poster.

Tatyana Suskin, a 26-year-old Jewish woman, was charged on Thursday with illegally posting the placards and with endangering life by stoning an Arab car on Saturday. The offences carry a maximum 24-year sentence.

Palestinians have demanded that Israel remove the 400 Jewish settlers who remained in fortified enclaves under army guard in the heart of the city of 100,000 Arabs after Israel turned over 80 percent of Hebron to PLO self-rule in January.
"I want to make one thing clear: We will continue to live here and we will continue to build," Hebron Jewish settler Moshe Ben Zimra told army radio.
